metadata.name: Latimore OS — Email Drip Campaign Engine
metadata.description: Source-tagged, six-stage 30-day nurture workflow for insurance prospects: welcome, education, social proof, soft ask, urgency nudge, re-engagement. Produces a paste-ready addendum for a Business + Marketing Plan, plus automation rules and KPI tracking.

nodes.label: 🧠 Business + Plan Context Lock
🏷 Source Tagging + Sequence Assignment Map
nodes.prompt:
Create the “Trigger Sources” section.

Use this structure:
- Lead Source
- Assigned Sequence Name
- Primary intent of that sequence
- CRM tag(s) to apply (source + sequence + stage)
- Entry criteria (what makes a lead qualify)
- Exit criteria (what stops the drip: booked, replied, opted out, closed)

If the user provides a mapping table, preserve it exactly and add the missing columns above. If not provided, generate a mapping that covers at least:
- QR code / community events
- Website consultation form
- Quote request
- Retirement / annuity inquiry
- Facebook DM keyword
- Google Business Profile

Make the tags consistent and copy-paste friendly for {crm_name}.

nodes.label: 🗓 30-Day Drip Blueprint
nodes.prompt:
Build the “30-Day Lead Nurture Sequence” section as a table.

Columns:
- Day
- Stage (welcome, education, social proof, soft ask, urgency nudge, re-engagement)
- Channel (email, text, both)
- Theme / subject angle
- Primary goal
- CTA
- Personalization tokens to use (use {crm_first_name_token} and {booking_link})

Rules:
- Day 0 must confirm receipt and set expectations.
- Education must teach a simple framework to help estimate coverage needs.
- Social proof must emphasize local/community credibility.
- Soft ask must invite a low-pressure review.
- Urgency must explain risk of waiting without fearmongering.
- Re-engagement must add fresh value and reopen the loop.

End with a short note on how to adjust timing if the lead replies or books early.

nodes.label: ✉️ Six Email Drafts (Plug-and-Play)
nodes.prompt:
Write the full copy for the 6 emails in the sequence.

Constraints:
- Each email includes: Subject line + body + clear CTA with {booking_link}
- Use {crm_first_name_token} in greeting
- Keep paragraphs short and scannable
- Voice: plain English, no pressure, clarity-first
- Include a consistent signature block:
  {sender_name}
  {sender_title}
  {business_name}
  {phone_number}
- Include minimal compliance footer language if {compliance_notes} requires it
- Ensure each email matches its stage goal and day

Output as:
Day 0 Email
Day 2 Email
Day 5 Email
Day 10 Email
Day 17 Email
Day 30 Email

nodes.label: 📲 Text Message Companions
nodes.prompt:
Create a matching set of SMS/text messages for Day 0, 2, 5, 10, 17, 30.

Constraints:
- 240 characters max each
- Friendly, professional, local-trust tone
- One clear CTA per message (either reply with a word, or book via {booking_link})
- Use {crm_first_name_token} where appropriate
- Include opt-out language if required by {compliance_notes}

Output as:
Day 0 Text
Day 2 Text
Day 5 Text
Day 10 Text
Day 17 Text
Day 30 Text

nodes.label: 🤖 Automation Rules + Manual Task Logic
nodes.prompt:
Write the “Automation Rule” section as an implementation spec for {crm_name}.

Include:
1) Trigger: new lead created and source captured
2) Actions immediately on entry:
   - apply tags
   - send Day 0 message
   - create a timeline for remaining touches
3) Conditional branches:
   - If lead books: stop sequence, move pipeline stage to Booked, create reminder task
   - If lead replies: pause automation for manual follow-up, move stage to Engaged
   - If lead opts out: stop all messaging, tag Opted Out
4) No-response rule:
   - If no reply and no booking after Day 10, create a manual task for {owner_name} with a short call script outline
5) Re-engagement:
   - At Day 30, tag as Cold if no engagement; optionally move to long-term nurture list

Output:
- A numbered rules list
- A compact pseudo-flow diagram in text (Lead comes in -> tags -> drip -> task -> pipeline move)

nodes.label: 📊 KPI Targets + Reporting Loop
nodes.prompt:
Create the “KPIs to Track” section.

Include a table with:
- KPI
- Target
- How to measure in {crm_name}
- Weekly action if below target (one specific adjustment)

Minimum KPIs:
- Email open rate
- Click-through rate
- Reply rate
- Booking conversion
- Sequence completion
- Cold lead revival

Then add:
- A simple weekly review checklist (10 minutes)
- Two A/B tests to run (subject lines and CTA phrasing)

Use {kpi_targets} if provided; otherwise propose realistic initial targets.

nodes.label: 🧩 Paste-Ready Marketing Plan Addendum
nodes.prompt:
Compile everything into a single “Email Drip Campaign System” addendum that can be pasted into a Business + Marketing Plan.

Structure:
- Overview (why repeated touches matter)
- Six-stage framework (welcome, education, social proof, soft ask, urgency nudge, re-engagement)
- Trigger Sources and Sequence Assignment
- 30-Day Lead Nurture Table
- Email Drafts
- Text Companions
- Automation Rules
- KPIs to Track
- Bottom Line (one paragraph summarizing: lead -> tag -> drip -> booking -> task -> pipeline)

Make it clean, skimmable, and implementation-ready.

keys.name: primary_offers
values: Life insurance, living benefits, mortgage protection, retirement income planning, annuity education, legacy planning

keys.name: voice_guidelines
values: Plain English, no pressure, clarity-first, trust-building, local community tone

keys.name: trigger_sources_table
values:
PAHS QR code -> Family Protection / Community Trust
Website consultation form -> General Protection Review
Ethos quote request -> Fast Term / Living Benefits
Retirement inquiry -> Annuity / Safe Money
Facebook DM “PROTECT” -> Life Insurance Education
Google Business Profile -> Local Trust / Policy Review

keys.name: compliance_notes
values: Include unsubscribe/opt-out instructions where required. Follow applicable TCPA/CAN-SPAM rules. Use business address/footer if required by your email provider.

keys.name: kpi_targets
values:
Email open rate: 35%+
Click-through rate: 3%–8%
Reply rate: 5%+
Booking conversion: 10%–20%
Sequence completion: 80%+
Cold lead revival: 5%–10%

keys.name: pipeline_stages
values: New Lead, Nurturing, Engaged, Booked, No Response, Closed Won, Closed Lost, Opted Out, Cold
